items.note: Annual report 2024-25 (published July 2025) says 18 chargeable off-street car parks in South Shields town centre and the Foreshore, pay and display, and the table rows add up to 2,145 spaces; 238 on-street bays (rows add up to 238); Hebburn Central 197, Mill Dam 170, Winchester Street 194 are in the free list. BUT the report's text says 22 free off-street car parks with total 1,431 spaces, while its table names 25 free car parks and the section totals (197+899+112+16+19) add up to 1,243, not 1,431 (the South Shields rows themselves sum to 952, not the stated 899). The 2023-24 report repeats the same 1,431 total with 23 car parks, so the figure looks stale or wrong. The draft repeats 22/1,431 as fact.
items.corrected_text: South Tyneside Council's 2024-25 parking annual report lists 18 chargeable off-street car parks (2,145 spaces) in South Shields town centre and on the foreshore, run by the council as pay and display, plus 238 chargeable on-street bays in South Shields. It also lists free off-street car parks in South Shields, Hebburn, Jarrow, Whitburn and Boldon (including Hebburn Central with 197 spaces, Mill Dam with 170 and Winchester Street with 194). The report's text gives 22 free car parks and 1,431 spaces, but its own table lists 25 and its section totals add up to about 1,243, so that count and total are not reliable.

items.note: All numbers check: Pierhead 292 spaces, 130,154.05 GBP; South Promenade South 129, 87,915.35; Charlotte Street (3 car parks) 134, 25,503.43; off-street income 1,334,286.18 (2024-25) vs 1,132,845.73 (2023-24); chargeable spaces 2,145 vs 2,212. NOTE the 2023-24 figures are from a different URL (publications.southtyneside.gov.uk/reports/parking-annual-report-2023-2024, published Sept 2024), which I also read; the cited URL only carries 2024-25. Problem: the claim that seafront car parks together outweigh the town-centre ones holds only for the itemised rows (seafront about 417,559 vs town centre about 107,437). The report also shows 'Additional Car Park Income' of 809,290.30 GBP (573,239 in 2023-24) that is not allocated to any car park, which is over 60 percent of the total. 'Biggest earner' must be limited to the itemised car parks.
items.corrected_text: Among the car parks itemised in the 2024-25 parking annual report, Pierhead earned most, with 292 spaces and 130,154 pounds of tariff income, ahead of South Promenade South (129 spaces, 87,915 pounds); Charlotte Street's three car parks with 134 spaces took 25,503 pounds. On the itemised lines the seafront car parks took about 418,000 pounds against about 107,000 pounds for the town-centre ones, but a further 809,290 pounds is listed as 'Additional Car Park Income' without being allocated to any car park. Total off-street tariff income rose from 1,132,846 pounds in 2023-24 to 1,334,286 pounds in 2024-25 (the 2023-24 figures come from the separate 2023-24 report), while the number of chargeable spaces fell from 2,212 to 2,145.

items.note: 2024-25 report tariffs column: seafront (Harbour Drive N/S, Pierhead, Pier Parade, South Promenade N/S, Dragon, Trow Quarry, Marsden Lea, Whitburn Bents) 1.20 per hour, 6.00 all day; town-centre (Charlotte St, North St, Salem St, Oyston St, Interchange, Thomas St) 1p per min for first hour, 4.00 all day. Mill Dam, Hebburn Central and the five Jarrow car parks are in the free list. 2023-24 report (separate URL, read) shows seafront 1p per min, 5 pounds all day. All as written; the 5-pound figure comes from the 2023-24 URL, not the cited one.

33 resident permit scheme rows (STR numbers) in the 2024-25 report; all named examples are on the list (Westoe Village, Beach Road, Broughton Road, Harton Moor estate, Grange Place Jarrow, South Drive Hebburn, North Road East Boldon). Introduction: aims to support economic activity and viability of town centres and local shopping areas and reduce congestion. 19,788 PCNs issued 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025. 15,282 for 2023-24 is confirmed in the 2023-24 report (separate URL, read).

Notice (Public Notice Portal, Shields Gazette; published and dated 11 May 2026) is a 'Notice of Variation' under RTRA 1984 ss35C/46A saying charges 'will be varied' with effect from 8 June 2026; it is not worded as a proposal, so 'proposed' is wrong. Seafront: 1.20 to 1.60 per hour, 6.00 to 8.00 all day, coaches and passenger vehicles free to 10.00 all day: correct. Town centre: current charge was 0.05 per 5 minutes (minimum 10p) for first hour then 1.00 per hour thereafter, 4.00 all day; amended to first hour free, 1.00 per hour thereafter, 4.00 all day; permits unchanged (432 per annum): correct, but 'per-minute charge' should be 5 pence per 5 minutes. Temple Park 60p to 1.00 all day: correct. The notice does not itself confirm the charges took effect; the 14 August notice lists them as current charges.
items.corrected_text: On 11 May 2026 the council published a notice of variation saying that from 8 June 2026 seafront car park charges would change from 1.20 to 1.60 pounds per hour and from 6 to 8 pounds all day (coaches and passenger vehicles from free to 10 pounds all day). In the South Shields town-centre car parks the charge would change from 5 pence per 5 minutes for the first hour, then 1 pound per hour, to a free first hour then 1 pound per hour, with 4 pounds all day unchanged and town-centre permits unchanged (432 pounds a year). Temple Park was to go from 60p to 1 pound all day.

items.note: Notice published and dated 14 August 2026 (Public Notice Portal): says that 'on Sunday 13th September 2026' charges at the listed locations 'will be varied'. Seafront car parks: current 1.60 per hour, 8.00 all day; amended 10.00 all day (8am to 8pm). Town-centre car parks: current first hour free then 1.00 per hour, 4.00 all day; amended first hour free, 1.00 per hour thereafter, 10.00 all day (8am to 5pm). Beach Road East/Beach Road on-street: 1.20 per hour, 6.00 all day, amended 10.00 all day. The notice states no reason for the change (no event is named). The cited URL is ONE notice only. I could not find or open the companion notice that supposedly varies charges back from Monday 14 September 2026 (portal search is JavaScript/postcode based; web search did not surface it), so that sentence is unconfirmed. Do not attribute a reason (a Gazette article reportedly links it to the Great North Run, but that was not opened and the notice does not say so).
items.corrected_text: A council notice of variation dated 14 August 2026 lists the current charges as 1.60 pounds per hour or 8 pounds all day on the seafront, and a free first hour then 1 pound per hour with 4 pounds all day in the town centre. It says that on Sunday 13 September 2026 the all-day charge at those car parks would be varied to 10 pounds (Beach Road East on-street bays from 6 pounds to 10 pounds all day, hourly rate unchanged at 1.20 pounds). The notice does not state a reason for the one-day change.

items.note: Notice (published 12 June 2026, dated 12 June): Order made 10 June 2026, in operation 15 June 2026; adds Station Road and McAnany Avenue car parks to the schedule of Town Centre Car Parks. Station Road: Mon-Sun 8am to 5pm, first hour free then 1.00 per hr, 4.00 all day. McAnany Avenue: Mon-Sun 8am to 8pm, 1.00 per hr, 4.00 all day. 'Following objections the proposed charges at Mill Dam Car Park will not be coming into effect and parking will remain free.' All as written.

Same notice. Contactless: the order adds contactless credit/debit card payment 'at ticket machines equipped to accept contactless card payments', so not all machines. Trow Quarry, Marsden Lea and Whitburn Bents closed 8.30pm to 8.00am: correct. Harbour Drive North and South and Parking Area A of Pier Head (smaller area facing mobile homes) no longer closed 10pm to 8am: correct.
items.corrected_text: The same order adds contactless card payment at town-centre and foreshore ticket machines that are equipped to accept it, and sets Trow Quarry, Marsden Lea and Whitburn Bents car parks to close from 8.30pm to 8am. Harbour Drive North and South and the smaller Pier Head area A (the one facing the mobile homes) are no longer closed from 10pm to 8am.

items.note: Council newsroom, 15 Jun 2026: 'From today (Monday 15 June), pay and display parking is now fully operational at McAnany Avenue car park and on-street bays', seven days, 8am to 8pm, 1 pound per hour or 4 pounds all day; aimed at ongoing parking issues in the Harton Moor area where long-stay parking limits visitor availability, particularly for hospital visitors. New card-only machines and PayByPhone at Temple Park replacing the previous system; charge remains 1 pound all day. Title matches.

Citizen Space page 'McAnany Avenue, South Shields - Pay and Display Changes' (results updated 24 Feb 2026; open 23 Jan to 13 Feb 2026): proposal for P&D at disused old Brinkburn area near the district hospital plus on-street bays on McAnany Avenue; 4 responses, 2 for, 2 against; answer A4 says a permit scheme is required to be guaranteed a space near your property. Proposed tariff 1/2/3 pounds for hours 1-3, 4 all day. NOT on this page: the Station Road consultation drawing 4 responses and the proposal to add Mill Dam and/or Station Road to the staff permit scheme. Those two statements are on the separate page haveyoursay.southtyneside.gov.uk/road-safety/station-road-south-shields (which I read: 4 responses, 2 for, 2 against; 'It is proposed that Mill Dam and/or Station Road be included within the Council's staff parking permit scheme'). Corrected text keeps to the cited page; the Station Road part is true but needs its own source URL.
items.corrected_text: The McAnany Avenue consultation (23 January to 13 February 2026) proposed pay and display on the unused old Brinkburn site and on-street bays near South Tyneside District Hospital, and received 4 responses, 2 for and 2 against. In reply to residents who wanted free parking, the council said a resident permit scheme would be needed to guarantee a space near their homes. The scheme was to go on to a legal consultation on a draft traffic order.

items.note: Citizen Space page: opened 8 Dec 2025, closed 5 Jan 2026. Proposal for permit parking in streets around the South Shields Foreshore; summer demand often exceeds availability; Permit Holders Only (8am-8pm) and Permit Holders or Pay & Display bays (8am-8pm); first resident permit free for the first year then 20 pounds a year; visitor permits 10 pounds per book of 25 daily permits (max 4 books); 'proposals may change, or may not go ahead'. The page also offers free permits for over-65s and disabled badge holders (not mentioned, no error). The page does not state an outcome.

Page 'We asked, you said, we did' is undated; includes an entry operational 09/12/24. Westoe CPZ: many residents not in favour, negative views significantly outweigh positive; 'No further action will be taken ... at this time'; 2021 census 67.2 percent of South Tyneside households own at least one car vs 78 percent nationally; 85 percent of consultation responders own one car or more. Date 2026-10 and 'read on 21 October 2026' wording are correct.

Hebburn table: 70 spaces, 4 accessible, free; Fellgate table 52, free; East Boldon table 64, free; Brockley Whins: pick-up/set-down area, 'no parking facilities'; Chichester: 'There are no parking facilities'. Jarrow: text says a car park with 80 unclassified spaces and 1 accessible bay operated by South Tyneside Council on Grant Street; table says 38 (platform 1 side), 2 accessible. The draft's Jarrow statement is accurate. Not flagged by the draft: Fellgate text says 53 unclassified + 2 accessible bays (table says 52 total) and East Boldon text says 54 + 4 accessible (table says 64 total), so those pages also contradict themselves. Pages are undated; the cited URL is only the Hebburn page, the other stations are separate pages.
items.corrected_text: Travel North East station pages (undated, read on 21 October 2026) give free Metro car parks at Hebburn (70 spaces), Fellgate (52) and East Boldon (64) in their car-park tables, although the Fellgate and East Boldon descriptive text gives 53 plus 2 accessible and 54 plus 4 accessible bays. Brockley Whins has a pick-up and set-down area but no parking facilities, and Chichester has no parking facilities. At Jarrow the text says a car park with 80 unclassified spaces and 1 accessible bay, operated by South Tyneside Council, is on Grant Street, but the same page's table gives 38 spaces (platform 1 side), so the true capacity is unclear.

items.note: nexus.org.uk/park redirects (301) to travelnortheast.uk/ways-to-travel/metro/information/car-parking/, a Travel North East page, not Nexus. It is undated. Text: 'There are major car parks at 10 suburban stations' (it does not say park-and-ride in that sentence, though it mentions 'stations with park and ride'); free parking on Sundays at the listed stations including Hebburn. Heworth is a separate page (travelnortheast.uk/station/heworth/), address 'Heworth, Gateshead, NE10': twin car parks operated by Gateshead Council; short-stay 70 unclassified bays (up to 2 hours 2.00, up to 4 hours 3.50, Sunday all day 1.50), long-stay 392 bays (up to 4 hours 2.20, up to 12 hours 3.10, up to 24 hours 4.20). Figures match. 'Just outside South Tyneside' is the draft's own gloss; the page says Gateshead. Tariffs are undated live-page values.
items.corrected_text: Travel North East's Metro car parking page (the nexus.org.uk/park address redirects to it; undated, read on 21 October 2026) says there are major car parks at 10 suburban stations and lists free Sunday parking at Hebburn among others. Heworth station, in Gateshead, has twin car parks run by Gateshead Council according to its station page: 70 short-stay spaces (up to 2 hours 2 pounds, up to 4 hours 3.50 pounds) and 392 long-stay spaces (up to 12 hours 3.10 pounds).

items.note: The Energyst, 15 December 2023: 'has entered a planned 20-year partnership with Connected Kerb to deliver 2,000 new charge points'; all 59 old units to be replaced; roll-out 'expected to begin in the new year' with chargers at 20 locations over the first two years; Connected Kerb to manage, maintain and operate; tariff for electricity currently subsidised by the council at 200,000 pounds a year; the council 'is currently negotiating' the pricing. The article says 2,000, not 'up to 2,000'; 'agreed' is slightly stronger than 'entered a planned partnership'. Single trade-press source.
items.corrected_text: In December 2023 trade press reported that South Tyneside Council had entered a planned 20-year partnership with Connected Kerb to deliver 2,000 new charge points, replacing all 59 old units, with chargers planned at 20 locations over the first two years. Connected Kerb would manage, maintain and operate them and introduce a tariff for electricity that the council had been subsidising at 200,000 pounds a year; pricing was still being negotiated.

items.note: GreenFleet, 14 Nov 2024 (council-reported): since work started in July 2024 new chargers installed in five car parks (22 extra sockets); rapid charging points 'will also be upgraded and adopted on to the Connected Kerb network across 14 locations, providing 15 sockets of 50kW': this is future tense, so 'had been moved' is wrong. Chargers 'set to be replaced at a further 33 locations to provide around 100 sockets by the end of summer 2025': OK. 'Only local authority in the North East yet to charge', 'more than two million k/w in free electricity since the first unit was installed in 2010' (the article writes k/w, not kWh). Up to 2,000 chargers over 20 years: matches. Council-supplied claims, not independently verified.
items.corrected_text: In November 2024 the council reported that, since work started in July 2024, new chargers had been installed in five car parks (22 extra sockets), and that rapid charging points at 14 locations (15 sockets of 50kW) would be upgraded and adopted onto the Connected Kerb network. Chargers at a further 33 locations (about 100 sockets) were to be replaced by the end of summer 2025. The council said it was the only North East local authority not yet charging for EV charging and had given away more than two million units of electricity (the article writes 'k/w') since 2010. No South Tyneside tariff or later progress figure was found.

corrected_summary: South Tyneside Council runs and prices the borough's off-street car parks itself. Its 2024-25 parking annual report lists 18 chargeable off-street car parks (2,145 spaces) in South Shields town centre and on the seafront, free car parks in South Shields, Hebburn, Jarrow, Whitburn and Boldon (the report's own count of 22 and 1,431 spaces does not reconcile with its table), and 238 on-street pay-and-display bays. Off-street tariff income rose from about 1.13 million pounds in 2023-24 to about 1.33 million pounds in 2024-25, though about 809,000 pounds of that is not allocated to any car park. A notice of variation dated 11 May 2026 set out changes from 8 June 2026: seafront prices of 1.60 pounds per hour or 8 pounds all day, and a free first hour in the town-centre car parks; an August 2026 notice lists those as the current charges and varies the all-day charge to 10 pounds for Sunday 13 September 2026 without giving a reason. A parking order made on 10 June 2026 and in operation from 15 June added Station Road and McAnany Avenue pay-and-display car parks, said the proposed Mill Dam charges would not take effect after objections, and added contactless payment at ticket machines equipped for it; the council newsroom reported McAnany Avenue and Temple Park cashless payment live on 15 June. Resident permit parking is already widespread (33 schemes in the 2024-25 report), a Westoe controlled parking zone was dropped for now after local opposition, and a seafront-area permit scheme was consulted on from 8 December 2025 to 5 January 2026 with no outcome found. Travel North East pages show free Metro car parks at Hebburn, Fellgate and East Boldon with capacities of 52 to 70 spaces, no parking at Brockley Whins and Chichester, and conflicting figures for Jarrow (80 in the text, 38 in the table); Heworth, in Gateshead, has Gateshead Council car parks. A 20-year Connected Kerb contract for 2,000 EV charge points was reported in December 2023 and progress in November 2024, with a charging tariff planned but none found. Much of the council's own site (southtyneside.gov.uk) was behind a bot-protection page on the research date, so several cabinet and press pages could not be read.
